Message Me Book a Discovery Call

You spent months in the lab or in the field, running experiments, debugging analyses, redoing what didn't work the first three times. Every data point cost you something. You've earned your results.

The tricky part isn't the science anymore. It's turning that pile of hard-won results into something that reads like a clear, convincing story.

Here's the thing: research is messy by nature! Things never go smoothly as we planned, the journey to your. results is full of unexpected turns. Yet, on paper it should unfold like a perfect story. Turning your work into a coherent narrative is genuinely hard, and it's something you'r expected to learn on the way.

Losing momentum during a PhD is very common. Feeling behind, stuck on the same paragraph for weeks, constantly questioning if you know what you're doing. This should not be price for becoming a researcher.

I've been there. I've had the good data and the manuscript that didn't do it justice. A narrative pulling in five directions at once, staring at my own draft at 11pm wondering what the paper was even trying to say anymore. I know that feeling from the inside.

After years of turning research projects into top-tier publications and helping students do the same, I know how important it is to have the right support, so you can successfully finish your PhD and enjoy the process. That's what I offer.

What if you could submit within few months, and feel the relief of moving on to your next, more exciting project?

What's it like to work with me?

  • • A fellow scientist who speaks your language. I've done the research, collected the data, revised, and published—I know how hard it is to publish a paper from start to finish.
  • • No judgment. A draft is never too messy, and no question is too basic. Bring me the chaos.
  • • Genuinely available. I won't vanish after sending tracked changes. Whether you need a full manuscript overhaul or just someone to think out loud with, I'm here.
  • • Feedback specific to your work. I take the time to understand your research, your argument, and where you want to go. I don't give generic feedback.

A manuscript shouldn't sit in a drafts folder for another six months. Your results matter—and the world can only build on work it can actually read. I built Morpho Editing because great science deserves to be told well. Let's make sure yours is.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much do your services cost?

Every project is different, and pricing depends on the scope of the work, timeline, and level of support required. I always provide clear estimates upfront and am happy to discuss different options to find the approach that best fits your needs and budget.

Do you offer student discounts?

I understand that students often work with limited funding. Whenever possible, I try to offer flexible solutions and adapt the scope of work to fit different budgets. Feel free to contact me to discuss your project and see what might be possible.

How quickly do you review projects?

I typically return projects within two weeks, though many are completed earlier. If a longer turnaround is necessary, I will always let you know beforehand and discuss the timeline with you directly.

If you are working under a tight deadline, please reach out as soon as possible. I will always try to accommodate urgent requests whenever possible. Additional rush fees may apply.

Will you review my project more than once?

Additional rounds of review can always be arranged depending on your needs. We can discuss the best approach before starting the project. Additional fees may apply.

About Me

Camille Le Roy, PhD

I'm Camille. Research scientist, field biologist, biomechanist — but above all, someone who understands the challenges of an academic career.

With a PhD in Evolutionary Biology from the University of Paris and over seven years of interdisciplinary research spanning ecology and biophysics, my path has taken me from the cloud forests of Peru to labs in France and the Netherlands. Along the way, I came to realize a struggle shared by many researchers: we're good at the doing — the experiments, the models, the fieldwork — but we struggle to hit 'stop' and immerse ourselves in the writing.

I’ve been on that road. I know that turning years of messy data into a compelling story is a long, eventful adventure. Having authored eight first-author papers in top-tier journals (including in Science, Nature Communications, PLOS Biology) and served as a reviewer for a range of multidisciplinary journals, I’ve learned the nuts and bolts of turning raw results into a manuscript that actually get published. There's a specific kind of thrill I get from taking messy, complex data and finding the story hiding inside it. It's one of my favorite parts of the work.

Besides research, you'll find me chasing a similar kind of flow state — on a skateboard, a snowboard, or trying (often failing) to stay upright on a slackline. Traveling is where a lot of this started, and I still find my best thinking happens far from a desk.

Why 'Morpho'?

During my academic journey, I studied the evolution of morphology and flight biomechanics in insects, particularly the iconic Morpho butterflies of the Amazon rainforest. My editing business takes its name from them.
